title: Quantum Fisher Information as the Speed Limit for Multipartite Entanglement
authors: Zain H. Saleem, Da-Wei Luo, Anjala M. Babu, Ting Yu, Stephen K. Gray, Anil Shaji
abstract: We derive a universal upper bound on the speed of multipartite entanglement generation. For arbitrary differentiable pure multipartite states undergoing parameter-dependent evolution, we prove that the rate of change of generalized concurrence is bounded by the square root of the quantum Fisher information (QFI). The proof follows directly from the symmetric logarithmic derivative formalism, revealing the bound as a consequence of quantum estimation theory, while a complementary Schmidt-spectrum analysis identifies the conditions for saturation and yields a tighter bound for rank-two bipartitions. We illustrate these results in interacting many-body spin models and investigate their behavior across the quantum phase transition of the transverse-field Ising model. At the critical point, we find that the QFI can be strongly enhanced while the generalized concurrence is nearly stationary and its sensitivity to the coupling is suppressed. This demonstrates that the enhanced parameter sensitivity associated with quantum criticality need not arise from rapid changes in the magnitude of multipartite entanglement.
summary: This work establishes that the Quantum Fisher Information (QFI) sets a universal upper bound on the speed of multipartite entanglement generation. By analyzing models like the TFIM, the authors show that while QFI can be strongly enhanced at quantum critical points, the rate of entanglement change may remain low. This reveals a decoupling between maximal parameter sensitivity and rapid entanglement growth.
main_problem: The paper derives a universal upper bound on the speed at which multipartite entanglement can be generated during parameter-dependent quantum evolution.
main_result: The rate of change of generalized concurrence is bounded by the square root of the Quantum Fisher Information ($\left| rac{dC_N}{dg}ight| \leq \sqrt{F_Q}$), demonstrating QFI as a fundamental speed limit for entanglement generation.
method: The primary proof utilizes the Symmetric Logarithmic Derivative (SLD) formalism from quantum estimation theory, complemented by Schmidt-spectrum analysis for bipartite cases.
model_or_system: The results are illustrated using interacting many-body spin models, specifically the Transverse-Field Ising Model (TFIM), and general pure multipartite states undergoing differentiable evolution.
key_observables: Generalized Concurrence ($C_N$), Quantum Fisher Information ($F_Q$), and the rate of change of concurrence ($ rac{dC_N}{dg}$).
important_parameters: The critical point of the TFIM ($g=h$) is investigated, where $F_Q$ is enhanced while entanglement change is suppressed.
main_assumptions: The general bound is not saturated away from the product-state boundary, although a tighter bound exists for bipartitions with Schmidt rank exactly two.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the dynamics of concurrence, its rate of change, and $\sqrt{F_Q}$ for the isotropic N-qubit Pauli interaction, showing $\sqrt{F_Q}$ acts as an envelope for the entanglement rate.
paper_structure: The paper first establishes the general bound using SLD theory, then analyzes saturation conditions using Schmidt decomposition, and finally applies these concepts to the TFIM to show that quantum criticality does not necessitate rapid entanglement changes.
why_interesting: It connects fundamental concepts from quantum estimation theory (QFI) directly to the dynamics of multipartite entanglement in many-body systems, providing a quantitative measure of how fast quantum correlations can evolve.
